I’ll replay the current public declarations and verify the manuscript and package versions first. Then I’ll use the checked interfaces to pursue the marked collar, disk saving, and Ricci-charge questions in parallel.

The six manuscript and PDF pairs, ten package checkouts, and nineteen nested pins match the previous milestone. I also found a checked ball-coverage theorem in the pinned geometry library. It lets us test charge transfer on a larger compact ball without assuming the comparison map already covers the charged source ball.

Lean has checked that compatible forward patches on the native trace suffice to cover the whole standard ball and determine its inverse. The disk calculation also gives a new obstruction. If the endpoint’s net saving must pay for a positive cap and the joined cost, a uniformly charged protected core eventually exceeds the available budget along a minimizing sequence. That conclusion allows the exterior charge to change.

I followed the supplied split and slid diagrams through their framed spectator and upper closing map. They give a standard-sphere control for the marking calculations. On the flow side, Lean now carries positive trace-free Ricci charge into a strictly larger ball of the pointed limit and proves the limit is noncompact when the initial volumes diverge. The final public build and independent replays are underway.

**Edition 03 reached milestone FOT-E43.** The main advance is a quantitative obstruction on the selected physical disk, together with a transfer theorem for the modified-flow alternative.

- **Physical disk.** A negative nonconformal first variation on a finite positive source gives a strict saving in both chiralities. If that net saving must also pay for a positive same-type cap and an additional joined cost \(j_s\), then the entire replacement disk satisfies \(\lambda_h^s(B)+j_s\le e-I\). On the selected minimizing subsequence, the protected original disk carries a fixed positive charge while \(e-I\to0\). Keeping that core therefore rules out this payment scheme at every sufficiently late index, even when the exterior changes.
- **Marked handles.** The actual inward extension and the height-calibrated product now compare on one two-sided collar, with explicit inverse transport and positive normal derivative. Compatible forward charts covering the native trace suffice to cover the entire independently marked ball and determine its inverse. For the supplied split and slid controls, Lean checked the framed torus coordinates, the split outgoing \(S^1\times S^2\) boundary, and the transported closing map. Constructing the compatible forward charts on a general selected edge remains open.
- **Modified flow.** Under the stated smoothing budgets and pointed-convergence hypotheses, positive trace-free Ricci charge survives in every strictly larger ball of the complete terminal limit. Divergent initial volumes force that limit to be noncompact. If it is a regular slice of a limiting Ricci flow with locally nonnegative scalar curvature in a time neighborhood, the charged ball contains a point of strictly positive scalar curvature.

All **73 new declarations** passed exact type and axiom checks, all 993 earlier public topic signatures reproduced, and both blueprint formats passed their link and source checks. Please review the work in papers/master and related sub-investigations, and also please review the new sub-investigation 05_collar_deformation_and_surgery. Please evaluate the current overarching research overview and plan for the formalization, and determine if it can be improved given the new work on the natural language side of the proof attempts.

I’ll compare the current master and collar-surgery manuscripts with the formalization overview, plan, and public Lean results. I’ll focus on whether the next formalization targets address the proof obligations that now matter most.

Two changes stand out. The new surgery work gives a direct recognition test on an intermediate three-manifold, even before positive-Yamabe entry. On the intrinsic side, E43 already proves what follows if sufficiently accurate positive caps exist. The missing formal step is to construct those caps from a physical collar with controlled geometry.

The new parent draft sharpens the first target. Its exact-face theorem treats both sides of a separating \(S^3\), including when neither side is initially given as a parametrized disk. I’ve incorporated that stronger statement into the assessment and identified the existing Lean results it can reuse.

**Yes. I recommend an Edition 04 overview and plan, keeping the existing formalization investigations and their owners.** Edition 03 still has the right proof structure, but its main plan opens with six tasks the register already records as completed. More importantly, Investigation 05 gives the program a route to smooth recognition from an actual handle presentation that can be pursued **before** establishing a four-dimensional energy bound.

I would make two changes to the research priorities.

1. **First formalization target: construct the positive caps from an exact physical face.** E43 already proves the energy consequence *if* suitable positive caps are supplied. The new manuscripts give the missing geometric argument for a conformally round, umbilic separating \(S^3\). At one fixed positive source with \(e<2T\), construct the deformation on its two actual collar widths, keep the joined path below \(2T\), and cap both complete sides in their original markings. The proposed Lean endpoint is that each side has equal raw chiral masses \(m_j^+=m_j^-=m_j\), with \(I^+(\widehat P_j)\le m_j\). On the selected charged disk this implies \(m_j\le e-I^+(M)\), excluding such a face at every sufficiently late index. This would close a named gap between the manuscript and Lean. [Parent manuscript](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/05_collar_deformation_and_surgery/manuscript/marked_collars_and_smooth_recognition.tex)

2. **Parallel topology target: recognize the closed manifold from either actual intermediate cut.** In the normalized mixed presentation, the winding-one-first test identifies \(S^3\), while the winding-zero-first test identifies \(\#_2(S^1\times S^2)\). Either can recognize the original smooth type. The supplied Mazur double illustrates why both orders matter. I would start Route 09 with one smooth marked cancellation carrying a residual framed tube and the upper closing map. The next application is already specified: with three middle handles, one qualifying prefix reduces the count to two, and a second qualifying prefix can recognize the resulting one-sided link presentation. A measurable sufficient test on an actual four-dimensional product band is \(\rho d^2\ge3\pi^2\), where \(\rho\) is its scalar-curvature floor and \(d\) its intrinsic width. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn134322468view0"}} [Surgery manuscript](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/05_collar_deformation_and_surgery/02_handle_isolation_and_marked_surgery/manuscript/recognition_from_marked_handle_cuts.tex)

**The overarching plan should distinguish the next Lean theorem from the next advance toward SPC4.** The exact-face theorem is my first choice for Lean. For broader coverage, the decisive questions are whether an untreated presentation supplies a qualifying cut, whether an arbitrary remaining smooth type admits subcritical entry, and whether an entered type supplies a controlled physical collar or a coupled repair on its charged region. I would retain the modified-flow route, with priority on constructing its smoothing inputs or using its singular initial end to constrain the original type. E43 already handles fixed-time charge transfer once the comparison is supplied.

An independent reader checked the two points most likely to change the proof’s scope: which marked prefix survives a handle reduction, and when a limit of positive metrics can establish entry or recognition.

Created **Edition 04** of the formalization program. The plan now starts from an arbitrary hypothetical nonstandard smooth homotopy four-sphere and asks what would settle that particular smooth type. Three outcomes suffice: a strict reduction of its minimum number of middle handles, direct smooth recognition, or a positive metric on the same type whose energy contradicts its defining infimum. **The open global problem is to produce at least one of these outcomes on every remaining type.** [Research overview](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/research-overview/04_OVERVIEW.md) · [Edition 04 plan](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/research-plan/04_PLAN.md)
